newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen rises to contract high on rumours.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen rises to contract high on rumours.

text.p: The key March three-month Euroyen futures contract rose to hit its contract high of 99.14 by Tokyo midday on Monday, aided by various rumours, traders said.

There was a widespread rumour that Japan industrial output for June will show minus four percent growth month-on-month, which is at the weakest end of market forecasts of minus 1.2 to minus four percent, they said. The data is due at 0430 GMT.

Another rumour, that financier Geroge Soros was beefing up his yen bond portfoliio while reducing his Tokyo stock holdings, added to the bullish sentiment of the yen debt market across the spectrum, traders said.
The March was at 99.13 at the end of the morning session, after rising to a contract high of 99.14. It closed at 99.11 on Tuesday.
Some said there was talk that a major Asian commercial bank placed heavy bids on March at 99.13 on the SIMEX.
Market sentiment was bullish from the outset due to news that Tokyo prosecutors suspected Yamaichi Securities Co Ltd paid 79 million yen to a "sokaiya" racketeer.
"Yamaichi's scandal will put the broker into an even more difficult financial situation than now, which may persuade the BOJ to hold down for a while," said a bank trader.

Yamaichi Securities has generally admitted to allegations of making payoffs to a corporate client widely known to be connected to a "sokaiya" racketeer, a government source close to the investigation said.
The Bank of Japan continued its accomodative stance in the money market through letting the market have some 300 billion yen surplus.
